summary: Assignments and the journal: a new workbench/assignments.py with seven registered Kernel operations (assignment.start, .plan, .step, .status, .stop, .resume, .list). An assignment holds the objective in the owner's words and a plan of steps, each with its tool and registered operation, its inputs with where each came from (stacy_hand origins, or an earlier step's output), the expected output, how it is verified, the grant it needs and its status (proposed, authorised, running, done, blocked, needs review). An append-only journal in the Kernel's database is written before each effect (PREPARED, committed) and after it (SENT, then DONE with the observation that proves it, or NOT_VERIFIED). A step is done only when its check verifies it; an effect with no check is never called done. Resume inspects every step first: a done step is checked still there and not redone; a prepared step whose effect is already there is recorded done and not made again; one whose effect is absent runs again only when that is safe; anything that cannot be told is left for the owner. Stop leaves "stopped by you" with what was done; Stop all / HALT (the work gate) holds it. Time left per step from her clock. The acceptance on Rail Demo was checked in one smoke script: 30 of 30 checks passed. Built, not tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad.

decisions: Own tables (asg_assignments, asg_journal, forward-only migrations) instead of the Night Shift's flow_* tables: a Night Shift order needs working copies, a Project Desk assignment and its fixed allowlist of work.* operations, which a K1 step over any registered tool does not fit. Reused instead: the Night Shift's work gate (work_trail held/epoch: Stop all and HALT hold assignments, a hold during a run stops it), its intent-before-effect discipline and its {"$step","path"} references, the Agenda (agenda.view rows, computed, no agenda_items rows so agenda.run_next never treats them as plain items), her hand (stacy_hand origins, bases, ALWAYS_ASKS, APPROVED_PICK) and her clock (brain_clock WINDOW/LEAST, price_ms).

Authorisation: a read step is authorised as it is planned ("a read never asks"); a change waits for the owner's press (assignment.plan authorise: needs the approve scope and the digest of the plan as shown). "all" never covers a change whose basis is the model's pick, one that always asks, or one the records mark for approval: those only by name. This is why step 3 reads "proposed" at the kill in the acceptance (it is authorised before resume).

"Recompute settled power" is office.datasheet.recheck (an approve-scope operation: authorised by name, inputs fixed at authorisation); "write a note" is files.write in her own area of Files (Slate/Rail Demo/Settled power note.txt), since a bounded step may write only there today; K3's grant ("edit files in Rail Demo/notes") can widen that.

Checks of an effect exist for reads (read again: same revision), files.write (digest on disk), office.datasheet.recheck (a new page replacing the old one, worked from the sheet as it is now, exact) and field.set (the cell holds the value). Any other operation can be sent but never becomes done (needs review); after an interruption it is "cannot tell" and is never repeated by itself. K2 widens assignments.CHECKS.
Before an effect is sent its expected output is looked for, on the first run too (an identical note already on disk is recorded done, not written again).

Time: a step's estimate is the plan's, else the median of this operation's measured times from the journal (at least 3 of the last 31, brain_clock's LEAST/WINDOW), else her clock's price for a model-turn operation, else a stand-in per kind of effect; whole ms, shown as 00:18; progress in whole percent.

One runner per assignment (flock on .ledger/assignments/<id>.lock); an interrupted step is found by its runner's process identity (operation_stop.process_identity) and the assignment will not run on until it is resumed (inspected).
Not continued while Graphite is closed (no service pump): resume is the owner's explicit word, as for the Night Shift.

release_note: Kasandra's assignments keep a journal. An assignment is your objective in your words and a plan of steps, each saying which tool it uses, where its inputs came from, what it should produce, how that is checked and what it needs from you. Reading never asks; every change waits for your word. A step is done only when its result is verified (the new page is there, the note on disk has the right digest). If Graphite is closed, crashes or you press Stop in the middle of a step, the journal says what was done and what was only prepared, and Resume looks before it repeats anything, so nothing is made twice. Each assignment shows its progress and the time left.
